knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson sets a repeatable route against the checklist, and separates actual defects from pre-existing damage and conditions outside scope.
The worked example records the limitation and asks for suitable access equipment rather than using a chair. The lesson says never to climb improvised platforms.
The detailed method says to follow a repeatable route, starting with access and hazards, and then inspecting each room or zone against the checklist.

practicalCriteria: Identifies defects systematically, avoids unsafe access, differentiates cleaning issues from damage and reports inaccessible areas.
Uses the authorised work order and site instructions
Recognises and escalates hazards or scope limitations
Records objective evidence and correction where needed
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Start with access and hazards, then follow the checklist room by room or zone.
Record of procedure step 6: Record facts rather than assumptions, including any area that could not be reached.
Record of procedure step 7: Report unsafe or inaccessible areas to the supervisor and request suitable equipment.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Confirm the work scope, the hazards and who can authorise any change before inspecting.
Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Start with access and hazards, then follow the checklist room by room or zone.
Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Inspect high areas only with suitable access equipment, never from an improvised platform.
